title: Evaluation and strategy provision to promote the indicators of Integrated Geriatric Care Program in Yazd County: A Participatory Action Research
content:
by Neda Sadat Nazaripanah, Haidar Nadrian, Neda Gilani, Mina Hashemiparast, Amirhossein Zebhi

Background

The growing aging population challenges healthcare systems worldwide, emphasizing the need for integrated geriatric care and continuous evaluation to improve key program indicators. This study aimed to evaluate and provide strategies to promote indicators of the Integrated Geriatric Care Program (IGCP) in Yazd County.

Methods

A Participatory Action Research (PAR) study with a concurrent mixed-methods design was conducted in Yazd, Iran, from January 2023 to August 2024. The study was carried out in six sequential steps within two action research cycles: (1) problem identification, (2) planning, (3) implementation of the Proposed Intervention Plan (PIP), 4) evaluating and revising the PIP, 5) implementation of the Modified Proposed Intervention Plan (MPIP), and 6) evaluation of the MPIP. The PIP and MPIP were each implemented over a four-month period. IGCP was evaluated before and after the action plan using the RE-AIM framework. Data were collected from Electronic Health Records and a researcher-made questionnaire completed by all healthcare providers (n = 9). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 26 and R software (version 4.2.2).

Results

The evaluation of the IGCP using the RE-AIM framework showed a progressive improvement in total standardized scores across the study steps: 54.05 ± 8.09 at baseline, 67.23 ± 5.89 after the PIP, and 81.98 ± 6.61 after the MPIP. The Complete Care indicator increased to 20.78% following the initial intervention. Repeated measures ANOVA and post hoc tests indicated a statistically significant difference in total standardized scores across the study steps (P < 0.001), and Friedman’s test confirmed significant differences among the five RE-AIM dimensions at each step (P ≤ 0.002). However, the reach dimension did not show a statistically significant change (P = 0.122).

Conclusions

The IGCP initially had weak reach indicators, and while most indicators and dimensions increased following the action plan, some changes, such as in reach, were not statistically significant. These findings highlight program challenges and provide guidance for policymakers and providers. The PAR approach may facilitate improvements in geriatric care through iterative feedback and adaptation, stakeholder engagement, and integration of community resources.
